newsitem.title: UK: Former UK minister says Major must rule out EMU.
newsitem.headline: Former UK minister says Major must rule out EMU.

text.p: Former British Treasury minister David Heathcoat-Amory called on Prime Minister John Major on Tuesday to rule out entry into a single European currency.

Heathcoat-Amory, who quit his government post this summer to fight moves towards European economic and monetary union, told a fringe meeting at the Conservative conference: "Let us rule out now British participation in a single European currency."
"The proposal to give up the pound is a constitutional outrage and would be an economic disaster," he said.

Heathcoat-Amory, the former Paymaster General in the Treasury, said that under a single currency, vital decisions on interest rates and monetary policy would be taken by a European central bank in Frankfurt, accountable to no one.

"What should worry all businessmen is that the single European interest rate, and a single monetary policy, cannot by definition take account of the specific requirements of the British economy," he said.
